own_solution.law: Moving-source Doppler shift: f' = f c/(c - v_s)
assumptions: source approaching along the line of sight

defect_reasons.other: T8B99 'The siren is then tuned up by a further 16 Hz' does not say whether the retuning precedes the listening asked about and sits awkwardly beside 'a steady tone of 440 Hz'; the authors' R reading (456 Hz emitted) is the most natural one but not the only one.

notes: Certified answers verified: 440*343/323 = 467.245; q = 9: 449*343/323 = 476.802; q = 16: 484.235; q = 24: 464*343/323 = 492.731 Hz. The authors' C derivation for the initial distance is correct: heard period = 1/f - vs/(f c), so d cancels exactly (valid while the source is still approaching, which holds at 180-950 m for the wavefronts concerned). In pass 1 I called the distance K; I now accept C as the better label since d enters the wavefront arrival-time relations and cancels, but the answer is the same and pass 1 is unchanged. Minimal pairs T5688/T8B99 (horn vs siren) and TEE83/TD410 (earlier run vs this measurement) share '16 Hz' and differ only in attachment/timing. Numeral-free twins TEDCB and T62DC as declared. T8B99 ambiguity kept at medium only; it does not make the item wrong.
